paper_title: Approximating Densest Subgraph in Geometric Intersection Graphs
statement: We presented two near-linear time approximation algorithms to compute the densest subgraph on (implicit) geometric intersection graph of disks. We conclude with a few open problems. Are there implicit geometric intersection graphs, such as unit-disk graphs or say, interval graphs, for which the exact densest subgraph can be computed in sub-quadratic time (in terms of n)? Finally, maintaining the approximate densest subgraph in sub-linear time (again in terms of n) under insertions and deletions of objects, looks to be a challenging problem (in prior work on general graphs an edge gets deleted or inserted, but in an intersection graph a vertex gets deleted or inserted).
